text:
Major League Baseball has seen more home runs over the past several decades, but those big hits haven’t brought more viewers to the World Series. Television audiences for MLB have dropped significantly since the 1970s, despite an increase in home runs. Data from Baseball Almanac and Baseball Reference show how baseball’s biggest event has struggled to bring in viewers.
Millions of people tuned in to watch the World Series in the 1970s. From 1973 to 1979, baseball’s biggest stage averaged approximately 36.3 million viewers, with the most being in 1978 with 44.3 million viewers. By 2023, that number had fallen to 9.1 million, showing a dramatic decline. The overall trend shows a steady decline in viewership over the past five decades.
While World Series viewership has plummeted, MLB teams have increased their home run rates. The data shows a negative relationship between home runs per team and World Series television viewership. Homerun’s still remain one of baseball’s most exciting plays, but hitting more of them has not reversed the steady decline of viewership.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)

batting <- read_csv("MLB_batting_1973_2026.csv")

ws <- read_csv("WS_ratings - Sheet1.csv")

joinbatting <- batting |>
  select(Year, HR, 'R/G') |>
  rename(runs_per_game = 'R/G')

joinworldseries <- ws |> 
  select(Series, Viewers) |>
  rename(Year = Series, ws_viewers = Viewers)

combined <- inner_join(joinbatting, joinworldseries)


combined <- combined |>
  mutate(viewers_millions = ws_viewers/1000000)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data=combined, aes(x=HR, y=viewers_millions), color="grey") +
  geom_smooth(data=combined, aes(x=HR, y=viewers_millions), method="lm", se=FALSE) + 
  geom_text_repel(data=combined |> filter(viewers_millions == max(viewers_millions)),
            aes(x=HR, y=viewers_millions, label=Year)) +
  geom_text_repel(data=combined |> filter(viewers_millions == min(viewers_millions)),
            aes(x=HR, y=viewers_millions, label=Year)) +
            
        
   labs(
    title="As Home Runs Increased, World Series Viewership Declined",
    subtitle="Despite more home runs per game the World Series has struggled to maintain its television audience",
    x="Home Runs Per Team Per Game",
    y= "World Series Television Viewers(Millions)",
    caption="Source: Baseball-Reference and BaseballAlmanac | Graphic by Blake Lorenzen"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

combined <- combined |>
  mutate(mean_viewers = mean(viewers_millions))

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data=combined, aes(x=Year, y=viewers_millions), color="orange") +
  geom_line(data=combined, aes(x=Year, y=mean_viewers), color="blue") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,50)) +
  geom_text_repel(data=combined |> filter(viewers_millions == max(viewers_millions)),
            aes(x=Year, y=viewers_millions, label=Year)) +
  geom_text_repel(data=combined |> filter(viewers_millions == min(viewers_millions)),
            aes(x=Year, y=viewers_millions, label=Year)) +
 labs(
    title="World Series TV Viewership Has Fallen Drastically since the 1970s",
    subtitle="After drawing more than 40 million viewers in the late 1970s, the World Series now attracts a fraction of that audience",
    x= "Year",
    y= "World Series Television Viewers(Millions)",
    caption="Source: Baseball-Reference and BaseballAlmanac | Graphic by Blake Lorenzen"
  ) +
   theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
     plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )









Baseball now has to compete for attention in a much different TV market than it did in the 1970s. There are more streaming platforms, social media, and channels that have changed how fans watch their favorite team. These changes help explain why world series television viewership. Despite the changing sport of baseball and more data tracking launch angles and power, the MLB has not found a way to bring its viewership to the titan that it once was. This creates a challenge for baseball, creating more exciting moments doesn’t necessarily mean more viewers watching at home.


Code
highlight <- ws |> 
  mutate(
    color = case_when(
      Series == 1978 ~ "High",
      Series == 1980 ~ "High",
      Series == 2021 ~ "High",
      Series == 1995 ~ "High",
      Series == 2004 ~ "High",
      TRUE ~ "Normal"
    )
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data=highlight, aes(x=Series, weight=Rating, fill=color)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("blue", "grey")) + 
  labs(
    title="Baseball has struggled to compete for attention in a crowded market",
    subtitle="Television rating for the Fall Classic has been on a steady decline since the 1970s. The blank spot is for the 1994\nseason where players went on strike and the series was cancelled.",
    x= "Year",
    y= "Television Rating",
    caption="Source: Baseball-Reference and BaseballAlmanac | Graphic by Blake Lorenzen"
  ) +
   theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
     plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
